metadata.title: Claude, Account Research.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude already knows what's going on with an account, or has to go find out, using the account-research skill's own trigger-phrase and pipeline rule as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill doesn't make Claude remember an account -- it makes Claude look, in the same steps, only when the words match its triggers.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 ('research Acme Corp' run through the same three-step pipeline, then run again unchanged; contrasted with a non-matching request that never starts it)

beats.narration_text: You ask Claude what's going on with an account, and it feels like it should already remember everything about it. It doesn't -- it has to go check first. So how does that checking actually work?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'You ask about an account. Claude must already remember it, right?', hesitates on 'remember', corrects to 'check'

props.text:
You ask about an account.
Claude must already
remember it, right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('remember' -> 'check') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: It's a reasonable guess -- Claude does hold a huge amount of general knowledge. But an account's signals change today: a new hire, a funding round, a product launch. None of that lives in anything Claude was trained on. Answering from memory alone would mean guessing, not researching.

shot.new_visual_element: A frozen 'trained on' date on a calendar; three signal cards -- new hire, funding round, product launch -- arriving after it, out of reach

production_viz.label: Nothing dated today is in memory
production_viz.mechanic: A calendar card on the left is stamped 'TRAINED ON' with a fixed date, then freezes -- no further marks land on it. To the right, three small cards draw in one at a time along a timeline running past that frozen date: 'new hire', 'funding round', 'product launch', each stamped with today's date. A dotted line from the frozen calendar toward the three cards fails to reach them and fades.

beats.narration_text: The fix is a SKILL.md file Claude reads before it acts -- instructions, not memory. It only fires when your words match its triggers: 'research a company,' 'what's going on with an account,' phrases like that. Say 'research Acme Corp,' and it runs the same three steps every time: read the file, pull the account's signals, return them.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- 'research Acme Corp' matched against the trigger list, then walked through Read, Execute, Return

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- matched, then walked step by step
production_viz.mechanic: A SKILL.md card sits at top with a short list of trigger phrases beneath it: 'research [company]', 'what's going on with [company]'. THE ANCHOR. The words 'research Acme Corp' type themselves out below, a bracket snaps to the matching trigger phrase, and the query flows left to right through three labelled stations -- READ, EXECUTE, RETURN -- lighting each in turn. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Run 'research Acme Corp' again next week, and Claude walks the same three steps -- that's what a written spec buys you: repeatable, not remembered. But phrase it outside the trigger list, some account question the file never anticipated, and the pipeline never starts. You're back to Claude answering from what it already knows -- the exact guess we started with.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the same query run again, identical steps; then a non-matching question that never enters the pipeline

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- same steps again, then nothing starts
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 SEQUENCE RETURNS, identical: 'research Acme Corp' flows through READ, EXECUTE, RETURN again, same lighted path. Beside it, a different, unmatched question types itself out, no bracket snaps to any trigger, and the three stations stay dark -- the query simply sits there, going nowhere. A line of small italic text appears beneath: 'no match. no pipeline. just Claude, on its own.'

beats.narration_text: account-research doesn't make Claude remember your account. It makes Claude follow the same steps to look -- only when your words match what it was built to hear.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. I want to research a company using the account-research skill. Read the skill file and walk me through what you'll do, step by step, before you do it. Watch for two things: does Claude name the exact trigger phrase your words matched, and does it lay out the steps before running them? Liam, in for Bear.
